worksheet.title: Which Way?
worksheet.subtitle: Choose the arrow that goes to the star
worksheet.learning_goal: I can choose the arrow that moves Bit toward the star.

parts.title: Pick the right direction
parts.text: ➡ moves Bit to the right. ⬅ moves Bit to the left. Look at where the star is, then pick the arrow that moves Bit toward it.

parts.title: Watch Bit — star is to the right
parts.note: The star (box 5) is to the RIGHT of Bit (box 3). So Bit should go ➡.

parts.title: Bit on box 2, star on box 5
parts.prompt: Which arrow moves Bit toward the star? Circle it.    ➡    ⬅

parts.title: Bit on box 4, star on box 2
parts.prompt: The star is to the LEFT this time. Which arrow moves Bit toward it? Circle it.    ➡    ⬅

parts.title: You try — Bit on box 5, star on box 1
parts.prompt: Which arrow moves Bit toward the star? Circle it.    ➡    ⬅

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Choosing the right direction is part of making a plan. The first thing a coder asks is: which way do I need to go?

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children choose the one arrow — right (➡) or left (⬅) — that moves Bit toward the star. Picking the correct direction toward a goal is the first planning choice in making a plan. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper and a pencil or crayon. You read each prompt aloud. Optional: tape a row of numbered boxes (and a star) on the floor so a child can walk the steps.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Bit on box 3, star on box 5: "the star is to the right, so we go right."
2. Do one together. Exercise 1 — the star is to the right; circle the right arrow.
3. Let them try. Children do Exercise 2 (star to the left) and Exercise 3 on their own.

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — circle the right arrow. Exercise 2 — circle the left arrow.
Exercise 3 — circle the left arrow (the star is to the left).

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: always choosing right. Ask "is the star on Bit's right or left?" first.
Make it easier: stand on the floor boxes and point your body toward the star.
Make it harder: ask both the direction AND how many steps to reach the star.
Make it active: face the star and step toward it to check the direction.

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children use directional language and choose a direction toward a goal.
In plain terms: choosing the right direction toward a goal.
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child answers by circling, numbering, or drawing arrows.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child circles the arrow that points toward the star every time.
